      Fix #3263
The following piece of code used to print 15, 9, 14, which should be 15, 15, 15. This PR fixes this issue.
#include <locale>
#include <fmt/format.h>

template <typename Char> struct numpunct : std::numpunct<Char> {
 protected:
  Char do_decimal_point() const override { return '.'; }
  std::string do_grouping() const override { return "\1"; }
  Char do_thousands_sep() const override { return ','; }
};

int main() {
  auto loc = std::locale(std::locale(), new numpunct<char>());
  auto i = fmt::format(loc, "{:15.6Lf}", 0.1).size();
  auto j = fmt::format(loc, "{:15.6Lf}", 1.0).size();
  auto k = fmt::format(loc, "{:15.6Lf}", 1e3).size();
  fmt::print("{}, {}, {}", i, j, k);
}

part.text:
Fixed. The bug was in `float_writer::write` (include/fmt/format.h:2664): in the `exp > 0` fixed-notation branch, the padding size counted thousands separators over the whole `significand_size` instead of just the integer part (`exp` digits), since `write_significand` only applies grouping to the integer part. This made localized outputs (e.g. `{:19.3Lf}`) one or more characters short when the significand spanned more digits than the integer part.

The fix matches the upstream resolution of this issue: pass `exp` to `grouping.count_separators`. Verified:
- The previously failing `locale_test.localized_double` cases in test/xchar-test.cc:441-443 now pass
- Full `xchar-test`, `format-test`, `format-impl-test`, `printf-test`, `posix-mock-test`, and `os-test` suites all pass
- A manual repro with `{:19.3Lf}` values (-119.921, 2194.139, 0.295, …) now produces uniformly aligned output
